notes.title: The Life and Suffering of Prince Jerian — a new narrative RPG from Schisma Games
notes.notes:
It is our pleasure to announce a new narrative roleplay adventure from the minds behind [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1272160/The_Life_and_Suffering_of_Sir_Brante/]The Life and Suffering of Sir Brante[/url]!

The Life and Suffering of Prince Jerian is a narrative roleplaying game that casts the player as the heir to the Blessed Arknian Empire, who must carve out a destiny for his nation. The world is grim, and the gods are eager to punish anyone who breaks their commandments. People live preordained lives, their fates sealed the moment they are born. It is up to the player to decide what kind of leader they will be: uphold the established order, or build a new kind of future.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2936290/The_Life_and_Suffering_of_Prince_Jerian/

You, Prince Jerian of House Tempest, must embark on a lifelong journey. It starts in your childhood, blissfully ignorant of your destiny, and continues into maturity as you take up a role you have been primed for since birth: emperor. As crown prince, you must not only understand your country and its culture, but also make many difficult choices that affect the fragile balance of powers in the Empire, and inside yourself. If you go where political circumstance and family obligations guide you, you risk losing yourself in the chaos. Can you keep yourself whole, or will you shatter?

Check out the trailer, which will give you some first impressions about the upcoming game!

[previewyoutube=LsJb0TVRytc;full][/previewyoutube]

In addition, to celebrate the official announcement of the game, we are releasing a special video address from the development team at Schisma Games, in which they will pull back the veil of mystery shrouding the contents of their upcoming title. Come watch!

[previewyoutube=RdUQLk17Vqo;full][/previewyoutube]

The game is currently in development. Wishlist The Life and Suffering of Prince Jerian now and subscribe to our newsletter to never miss an update!

notes.title: Feedback on the very first Blind Fate: Edo no Yami demo & plans for the future!
notes.notes:
皆さん、こんにちは! It took us some time to process your feedback on the very first Blind Fate: Edo no Yami demo, but we are now finally ready to answer your questions.
In this article, we’d like to address some of the concerns most frequently voiced via the feedback form and give a brief account of the current state of Blind Fate: Edo no Yami development as well as our plans for the future.

[previewyoutube=mmOqdYwiMVs;full][/previewyoutube]

In case you missed PAX Online 2021 and haven’t tried the Edo no Yami demo yet, we suggest you click the “Wishlist” and “Follow” buttons on our official Steam page so that you will be notified when the demo becomes available again as part of the [url=https://www.gamescom.global/]gamescom 2021[/url] event.

All right, enough with the introduction! Moving on to your feedback.

[h3][b]Controls & controller support[/b][/h3]
Players can choose the preferred method for playing Blind Fate: Edo no Yami: with mouse and keyboard or with any of the supported controller models, though we genuinely suggest using a controller for the best gaming experience possible. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38712129/330aea6fa11d482c1fbb55a1f8fcc47de002f00e.png[/img]

Some of the early beta players reported problems with Xbox controllers, while others mentioned they would love to have a way of rebinding keys. The latter option has already been implemented, so we hope to hear about your updated experience once the latest demo has been released.

[h3][b]Technical issues, optimization, and performance [/b][/h3]
The game is mid-way through the development process and still has about half a year ahead of it, so we’re currently focusing on essential features, combat mechanics, etc. Once those are ready, we’ll move on to polishing and optimizing the game. Regarding minor technical issues such as FPS drops, you can expect them cleaned up in the next demo.

[h3][b]Combat mechanics[/b][/h3]
We have received numerous questions and suggestions from early demo players regarding combat mechanics and whether we plan to improve them. Obviously, having a fluid combat system and responsive controls is essential for an action platformer, so you can believe we have studied dozens of games from the same genre, aiming to learn from the best! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38712129/12947e9970b8d3971ceb8f58987189d5c1ddff2f.jpg[/img]

Players will be able to unlock dozens of special moves later in the game (stomps, dashes, dodges, special katana attacks, special cannon shots, etc.) by upgrading Yami’s skills at the Skill Tree. “Will it be possible to throw an enemy into the air?” you may ask. Yes, it totally will be with the Uppercut move. “What about dodging and counter-attacking after a parry?” Yes, we’re working on those as well!

Several users mentioned that performing finishers takes too much time, so we would like to address this point next. Finishers are not mandatory, it’s something that players can use to kill enemies in the most cinematic way possible, provided they have collected 100% of the data for the particular enemy type. Every finisher is a QTE (Quick Time Event) sequence and requires direct player input. This is why finishers are bound to take a bit of time, and it will most likely stay this way in the full version of the game.

What will be improved in the future, however, is the timing for parrying attacks and the lack of feedback from certain in-game opponents. 

[h3][b]Difficulty level[/b][/h3]
Blind Fate: Edo no Yami was never envisioned as a proverbial walk in the park. You are a BLIND samurai fighting for justice in a ruthless post-apocalyptic world, after all! We understand that some players want to speedrun the game while slashing enemies left and right, but we also want the project to offer a degree of challenge! Different levels of difficulty are planned for the final release, offering players a chance to learn the intricacies of battle through gameplay and in-game tips.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38712129/13dca3bdcf42cf849fbe2bc4c68a07d55b72dfc1.jpg[/img]

[h3][b]Official soundtrack and localization[/b][/h3]
Don't worry, we have this aspect of the game covered! If you have followed Blind Fate: Edo no Yami for some time now, you probably know that we partnered with an incredibly talented composer and sound designer, Joe Kataldo, who not only helped us with the previous project Hyperparasite but also has extensive experience working on TV and numerous gaming projects, including Terminator: Salvation VR.

[previewyoutube=e7ebPS73aPk;full][/previewyoutube]

Currently, we’re finishing the game’s powerful main theme that shall feature world-class cellist [url=https://tinaguo.com/]Tina Guo[/url]. Here’s a sneak peek (please, press on the button below to watch a Twitter video):

[url=https://twitter.com/Tinaguo/status/1414025107148660741 style=button][b]Watch video on Twitter[/b][/url]

We are thrilled to confirm that Blind Fate: Edo no Yami will not only be fully localized into Japanese but also feature a dozen other languages - all of the supported languages are currently listed on the Blind Fate: Edo no Yami Steam page.
____________________________

We’d like to thank you for your continued support and interest in Blind Fate: Edo no Yami. You've given us plenty of well thought out points and this means the world for a small crew like ours. Thank you for your feedback, don’t forget to follow & wishlist us on Steam if you want to stay tuned!

notes.title: The Dojo
notes.notes:
Today we will take a closer look at an important in-game location - the Dojo. In Japanese culture, a dojo is a place for meditation and spiritual learning as well as honing one's martial prowess and combat skills. Both in the real world and in the game, the Dojo is a place where a hero can train and prepare for future challenges.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38712129/7d8f265beef1e7b45ad1fd2fcbb0fffe615c8197.jpg[/img]

The great Skill Tree grows by the Dojo. It can be accessed to select and upgrade the powers you wield or check which abilities can be learned in the future.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38712129/7d89304ed781baa145e2d8b1497bc20519fcef45.jpg[/img]


Enter the Dojo to start a training simulation and battle challenging opponents.

[previewyoutube=zzEfl35WXPQ;full][/previewyoutube]


Here you will also meet those whom Yami could call his allies.

There are three of them: Tengu, Doggo, and Tancho. 

Let’s start with Tengu.
In Japanese mythology, the term Tengu (“Heavenly Dog”) can refer to a number of creatures. For example, Kotengu, also known as Karasu Tengu, Daitengu, or Yamabushi tengu. We'll be focusing on the Daitengu as it specifically served as a basis for the character players will encounter in the game. Daitengu literally means “Big Tengu.” It so happens that the Daitengu had taken on the role of human protector. This Tengu can take on many different forms: man, woman, child... But his main guise is that of a barefoot wandering old hermit, a Yamabushi monk, with a disproportionately long nose. It is believed that the length of the nose serves as an indicator of the particular Daitengu's power.

[url=http://yokai.com/daitengu/][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38712129/c7c1d8fa44e696c197d3ae9f8f224f114ef8be88.png[/img][/url]

The in-game Tengu is an AI that was originally running a garrison of Tengu battle models, a kind of a robotic SWAT team. For reasons unknown, it later found itself having to inhabit one of the said models and withdraw from worldly affairs.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38712129/220575d78f9f35b88dab63d7253a020b2c2e4be2.jpg[/img]

Yami have made the following note about the Tengu:
“Tengu can be difficult to understand. Sometimes it’s as if I were talking to a child, but then it looks at me, and I can feel the weight of gods-know how many centuries on its shoulders. It's an AI... Who’d ever thought I’d get to meet one. Everybody’s heard the rumors. AIs aren’t like machines at all - they think as human beings do or even better if legends are to be believed. Some are crazy and evil, but Tengu is one of the good ones. I mean truly, deeply good. It cares for the plants and animals, for everything around it. For some weird reason, it also cares about me. Maybe it's just lonely and needed someone to talk to.”


Besides Tengu, the Dojo houses a giant pet known as the Doggo. It's one of Tengu's creations that doesn't have a prototype in Japanese mythology. 

Here’s what Yami has to say about the mechanical canine:
“I don’t like machines. No, scratch that - I hate them. But those things at the Dojo, they’re... different. Tengu built them. It told me that they have something called an “Identity Core,” which holds and evaluates memories allowing them to forge a personality. This one’s just a dog, it even acts like one. I may not like machines, but you gotta be a special kind of asshole to hate dogs, so...”

[previewyoutube=SgDaD13RfU0;full][/previewyoutube]

The third robotic inhabitant of the Dojo, the Tancho Crane, also doesn't originate from Japanese folktales. However, the red-crowned cranes were often depicted as loyal companions to the samurai of old, with some legendary birds rumored to have lived for over a thousand years!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38712129/74317cc3208553c28f04049b8da069c894067ebc.png[/img]

Tancho is another one of the "living" robots created by the Tengu AI.
 
Yami describes it as follows:
“It's much more reserved than Doggo, but I have to be nice to it anyway. When Tengu told me that this thing could fly me around, I didn’t think much of it. Then we soared through the sky, and I couldn’t see a damn thing without the data, feeling my feet dangling in the air as we rushed through pure darkness. I could not steer, couldn’t do anything. The moral of the story is: this crane could have killed me anytime it wanted. If I want to finish my mission, I gotta stay on its good side, so that it does not drop me into the abyss when nobody’s looking.”

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38712129/e5b9e0c9ac70e2a41636468825c2aa7a3555d602.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Yokai Biome1: City of Ghosts
notes.notes:
The world of Edo no Yami consists of a number of different territories known as biomes. In this article, we are going to introduce you to the inhabitants of the very first biome available in-game - the City of Ghosts.

As was mentioned before, all the monsters of Yami no Edo are creatures from Japanese myths and legends, reimagined in futuristic cyberpunk style. 

In Japan, there is a legend that tells of the souls of peasants that haunt the rice fields they once tended to. Their name, Dorotabo, can be translated as "mud monks of the rice fields." 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38712129/9385e777b1ac5beac3a67873d260b629a3e75021.jpg[/img]


These poor creatures toiled away cultivating the fields, only to witness their life's work fall into desolation when the new owners neglected the farmland. The Dorotabo were often described as one-eyed, three-toed humanoid figures that lurked in the mud of the rice paddies, with their three remaining fingers symbolizing the mortal vices of anger, greed, and ignorance. They became especially active at night when the yokai crawled out of their hiding spots to hunt for the people who caught their ire. They are wrathful and vengeful spirits that seek to punish the careless and the negligent. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38712129/945ddb9d2de6b6e76b83e3285ffd3d5728b6ce14.jpg[/img]


The Dorotabo roam the unkempt fields, howling curses wherever they go. In the dark of the night, their malformed figures can barely be discerned among the stalks of rice as they pursue the new landowners or besiege their homes, robbing the living of sleep and slowly driving them insane. The yokai will not yield until the paddies that once fed them and their families are restored or until the new lodgers either die or flee the decaying estate.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38712129/eafd78ae9b8b63e51d051f5fd932ff9cf0f40495.jpg[/img]


In Blind Fate: Edo No Yami, the Dorotabo were reimagined as androids who have been discarded by their owners over 500 years ago, ending up in a junkyard. They drag their metallic bodies across the ground, reaching out to their would-be victims with arms that end in three clawed fingers.


[previewyoutube=qlONfnIeO9E;full][/previewyoutube]

The Dototabo rely on melee attacks. They grab onto their opponents and activate a self-destruct sequence that deals tremendous damage.

For your enjoyment, we provide a detailed concept art of the enemy.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38712129/1e19aafd1a21d42b605dd61e93a54c5eee014d92.jpg[/img]




Another one being’s name means “dirt licker.” In Japanese mythology, the Akaname are small, goblin-like yokai that live in the dirtiest corners of residential buildings and public baths.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38712129/754d9fc1c3bdf585ab600b90c39caef36c67de10.jpg[/img]

As tall as a child or a dwarf, the Akaname appear to be even shorter due to their typically bad posture. Their skin and hair seem to be covered in foul-smelling oil and may vary in coloration from unpleasant green to disgusting pink. 

Possessing either one or two eyes and a varied number of fingers on their hands and feet, the Akaname sport long tongues that they use to sweep filth around the floor of whatever place they came to inhabit. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38712129/2d07bb4d2dab83fc52afb7d86f425e1e32fa6bd7.jpg[/img]

Being pests, the Akaname hate house cleaning and quickly disappear the moment the house owners start taking hygiene seriously. These yokai are also easily scared and scatter away like cockroaches if someone shines a bright light in their direction. It is said that the Akaname spread diseases even better than plagued rats, so it's recommended to keep one's dwelling in good conditions lest you invite these beasts into your home.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38712129/5fb51f48ce75fc6df65dfa8a47d50f82cabb85ec.jpg[/img]

The in-game Akaname are cleaner bots that move on four legs and use their tongue-like cords to sweep the floor, move pules of debris around, or pierce and bleed out uninvited guests. 

[previewyoutube=jCeDHHG34WY;full][/previewyoutube]

This mechanical version of the yokai specialize in melee attacks. They can lash out with their "tongues" or grab Yami with a quick and unblockable motion.

Here is a concept art for these unusually dangerous janitors.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38712129/a1086c5b881bcc8782b40da6e34ba4f0b8e1f661.jpg[/img]

Wa nyūdō is a yokai whose name can be translated as the “wheel monk” and that is usually depicted as a gigantic human head, stuck inside a burning carriage wheel.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38712129/567c91228a55392553b381cbab6ac6b9dc43f32f.jpg[/img]

The Wa nyūdō are servants of evil who spend most of their time among mortals, always searching for new sinners to punish. Since these demons are constantly suffering from their own inextinguishable flame, they seek to extract at least a minor degree of comfort by inflicting similar pain on others. Should the Wa nyūdō encounter a suitable victim, they grab it with their teeth and drag the poor soul to hell to administer unspeakable punishment. Then the monster returns to earth, forced to continue the terrible cycle until it has paid its own karmic debt from previous lifetimes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38712129/7b10d1da00486e9822326522da8bee07268b1c79.jpg[/img]

Whenever there are rumors of Wa nyūdō sightings, wise people cancel all traveling plans and stay indoors to keep out of the yokai’s way. If one has to leave the house at such an hour, they would do well to wear protective amulets, since a mere glimpse of the evil spirit could bring misfortune to that person's entire family.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38712129/35d1d3c6dbd61141ab13a4d60aee56661d8e82df.jpg[/img]

In Edo no Yami, the Wa nyūdō are malfunctioning police units that dash and maneuver around decrepit roads, attacking perceived intruders on sight.

[previewyoutube=kM5iqpRwi3E;full][/previewyoutube]

They are dangerous foes, capable of both close and long-range unblockable attacks. Dodge the Wa nyūdō's projectiles and be ready to jump out of the way whenever they try to ram you. 

That’s it for now, but before you go - check out the Wa nyūdō concept art.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38712129/fd4cc4f53e070e62a2bf3b0ee75652ad485131e0.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Yokai. Myths and… reality?
notes.notes:
There was always a special place in Japanese folklore for thousands of mythical creatures - yokai, spirits, demigods, etc. Both in ancient times and in the age of technological progress, the Japanese made offerings to pacify the spirits and receive blessings from various deities. We cannot even for a second imagine that in a distant future, when robotics will change our lives forever, that they will stop believing in yokai in Japan. In this article, we will tell you about some of the creatures that made it into the game and show you how they will look in the futuristic world of Blind Fate: Edo no Yami.


Jubokko, also known as a tree child, a shrub offspring, or a vampire tree.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38712129/0a6261a24f99e72291d0914d998828076ba435d0.jpg[/img]

When viewed from faraway, these spirits appear to be just ordinary trees, growing in large numbers across fields that once served as sites of bloody battles and massacres of old. Very few can tell them apart from normal vegetation typical for the local climate, but should one try to dig under such a tree they will undoubtedly find a mass grave of human remains. This is ill-advised, however, since the Jubokko, poisoned by human anger and murderous intent, have themselves become blood-thirsty demons that will attack anyone who gets too close!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38712129/cb4bf0bcd1751904c79ab4837cefc4bd6dbde8a5.jpg[/img]

Jubokko often prey on unsuspecting travelers that stop to rest and shield themselves from rain or the sun's scorching rays under the crown of these cursed trees. They grab and claw at their victim's flesh with powerful branches that have sharp, finger-like outgrowths, then drink their blood, leaving a drained carcass for the wolves and other wild animals to feast upon.

In the world of the future, the Jubokko trees have changed quite a bit, but remain true to their nature: partially mechanized, they still thirst for the blood of anyone careless enough to get close to these menacing beings. Unlike the mythical Jubokko of old, however, the trees in-game have also learned to attack their enemies from a distance.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38712129/c2d1d058ea346f0b6e135e34a7d4baa18c2eea72.jpg[/img]

The Jubokku possess three distinct attack methods: they can throw stones, smash their branches on the ground, or perform a sweeping motion with their “arms,” damaging anyone standing nearby. Moreover, the last two attacks cannot be parried! Your hero’s only option is to dodge the deadly blows of the bloodthirsty Jubokko trees.

[previewyoutube=IeG5Q0lUVY0;full][/previewyoutube]


Itachi
Itachi is the Japanese name of the animal known as a weasel in the English language. Said to be the bearers of ill omens and sometimes even described as minions of witches as well as other evil forces, it is no wonder that the little mammals have landed their likeness to another fearsome yokai in the local bestiary. Just like their famous foxy counterpart, the Kitsune, Itachi were said to possess shapeshifting powers.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38712129/be9adee4af2e938490facabdbad3b1677bf30365.jpg[/img]

Unlike the many-tailed vixens, however, Itachi generally avoided direct human contact. Quite often, the only indication that something bad was afoot would be the cries of weasels heard around the nearby forest as if the little tricksters were chanting spells or passing along some important message. Seeing an untransformed Itachi was especially dangerous since they were said to be able to dominate a human's mind, forcing them to perform acts of great atrocity... or sometimes just bring the weasel and its friends some food if the victim was lucky enough. Large congregations of Itachi were also often blamed for starting wildfires as they were believed to have a habit of jumping on each other's shoulders, with the resulting "living totems" then summoning flames wherever they went.

In some regions of Japan, an even more dangerous cousin of this yokai, the Kamaitachi, could be found. These beasts have adapted to the cold mountain climate and learned to control devastating whirlwinds.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38712129/736bbc9133c64174cbc94b4deb456fe244d91908.jpg[/img]

Their claws are as strong as steel and sharp as a razor. Their fur is prickly, like a hedgehog’s, and they bark like dogs. Kamaitachi's movements are so fast that they become invisible to the naked eye. They come and go with the wind, leaving only death and devastation in their path.

In Blind Fate: Edo no Yami, Itachi are robotic weasels with razor-sharp blades attached to their paws. “Kill or be killed!” is the only philosophy these monsters understand.

[previewyoutube=YDs76wd6c6Q;full][/previewyoutube]

Itachi use two types of attacks: a claw strike and a spinning maneuver that hits multiple times and cannot be parried.

[previewyoutube=ktaa2mRqKu8;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: A few words about the game and its inception
notes.notes:
[i]Today we take a closer look at Blind Fate: Edo No Yami - the idea behind the project, its post-apocalyptic themes, the influence of Japanese culture on the game’s lore, as well as the progress so far. For this purpose, we have turned to the development team and asked them to answer some introductory questions.
If you enjoy this format, feel free to write your trickiest questions to the developers in the comments below and we will make sure to relay them in the future. :)[/i]


[b]Please tell us a little about your team.[/b]

[url=https://www.troglobytesgames.com]Troglobytes Games[/url] is an independent studio based in Barcelona.
There are not very many of us, but some members of the team have more than 20 years of experience in the game industry and worked together for other companies.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38712129/1521114aefecbc12fc5aeeb6862364c2bbc05654.jpg[/img]

In 2015, with the arrival of new young talents, guided by the passion to give shape to new ideas and to deliver new gaming experiences, we decided to move forward and to work on our own projects.
In 2020 we released our flagship title [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/838110/HyperParasite/]HyperParasite[/url], a roguelite twin-stick shooter set in the roaring 80s.

Now we are working on Blind Fate: Edo no Yami - a game about a blinded cyber samurai. The development is carried out jointly with [url=101xp.com]101XP[/url].


[b]
What served as your inspiration when choosing the setting for your game?
[/b]

We usually look back for inspiration to old arcade games - we have an arcade machine in our studio from which we extract the most interesting ideas.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38712129/9703022e0c4d733791de1eeb615a52dd5271dbbf.jpg[/img]

With those references we build up new assets, both in mechanics and visuals, to match a modern gaming scenario.


[b]
What made you put an emphasis on post-apocalypse and cyberpunk genres?[/b]

A post-apocalyptic world is a good setting if you want to have the player exploring a world where the old and the new are "present" at the same time.
The cyberpunk setting allows it to have deeper lore in the form of data and implanted devices such as hi-tech sensors.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38712129/61ad0baa84c2b201c10ee589ba95c56d635e885f.jpg[/img]

Yami, who is blind, can receive environmental data through tech wired directly to his brain, making him able to navigate complex levels.


The acquired data being old and incomplete, it sometimes does not accurately represent the real world: certain paths may not be what they seem and there is still much to discover.
Yami can obtain new data through his sensors and collect memories from defeated robotic opponents, allowing him to more clearly perceive the world he has to explore.



[b]Why Japan and not, for example, China? Tell us about your passion for Japanese culture and mythology.[/b]

We grew up watching Japanese animation from the 70s and the 80s. They served as an introduction to a foreign culture, its values and legends.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38712129/b81228c9a6addaeb1df68f24ff1c8723cb5cb2ce.jpg[/img]

In some of those cartoons, just like in Blind Fate: Edo no Yami, the protagonist’s adversaries were machines shaped like the creatures from Japanese folktales.



[b]What is the meaning of the “samurai way” in the game? That is, how important is this concept here compared to, for example, historical reality?[/b]

We imagined that post-apocalyptic Japan could witness the rise of a new samurai period.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38712129/0425b82f5c3ea82b1c32dd9c8c302c2ceb5ba5d4.jpg[/img]

Due to forced isolation from the rest of the world and the need to have loyal champions to protect the survivors, the old class of noble warriors was reborn and Yami represents his brothers in arms quite perfectly: endlessly loyal to his Shogun, he knows that his role is to obey and oppose the ever-present mechanical menace.



[b]Who served as the prototype for the main character? Does the protagonist share any traits with a member of the development team or maybe a notable historical figure? Are the players supposed to see something of themselves in their in-game alter ego?[/b]

Both as a game and as an individual character, Yami is a mix of different references originating in video games (Strider, Mark of the Ninja, Shinobi...), movies (Zatoichi and Blind Fury), and animes.
Another trait, especially noticeable during in-game dialogues and cutscenes, is his sarcasm which might have been inspired by someone on the development team, but we are not going to point any fingers…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38712129/816f29bd8ded8349a2f2b4e83ff09ed6d32d0a16.jpg[/img]

Players will discover more of the New Edo as Yami makes his way through the game’s story and, perhaps, even sees things from different perspectives.	



[b]What determined the choice of the particular engine used for this game? Did it offer the best prospects when it comes to high-quality graphics or was it something else?[/b]

We've been using Unreal Engine for the past 6 years and have also developed and published HyperParasite with it, so when the time came to decide what engine to use for this new project it was a no-brainer. UE4 allows us to express our full potential when it comes to graphics, atmosphere, etc.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38712129/1d4341ba7332a3728ed9a8f3bfcd4fcbd1ba5901.jpg[/img]



[b]What stage of the development are you currently on?[/b]

We're not operating in a linear fashion when it comes to certain aspects of the game - some of us are already working on more advanced parts of the story/gameplay, while the core mechanics have already been implemented and are presently being polished and expanded upon. There could even be a playable demo released sometime in the nearest future.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38712129/413d51c1e944b65f26d9ad7dbfa7e53b5c3bee24.jpg[/img]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1294880/Blind_Fate_Edo_no_Yami/

[b]If you wish to see more of the game before the release date, we have recorded an exclusive playthrough stream that will be held on September 17 starting from 9 PM BST.[/b]
To join the stream, please navigate to the Blind Fate: Edo no Yami page at a scheduled time and prepare to dive into the neo-noir retrofuturistic world of the game.

[b]Check the brand new gameplay trailer:[/b]

[previewyoutube=oC9B_Z4qAb8;full][/previewyoutube]

Blind fate: Edo no Yami is an action 2.5D platformer where you walk the dark path of a blind cyber-samurai in a world filled with robotic Japanese folktales. You are Yami - a bionic creature of metal and hatred. Your duty is to enforce the law and protect citizens from bloodthirsty robotic monsters known as the Youkai. A single mistake cost you your sight so you must now learn to “perceive” the world in a new way using your sensors.

The game is currently under development and is planned for release on PC, Switch, Playstation, Xbox in 2021. [b]Add it to your wishlist now and be sure to follow our latest news[/b] on [url=https://www.facebook.com/games101xp]Facebook[/url] and [url=https://twitter.com/games101xp]Twitter[/url]!
